html:
The palaces of the kings of Dahomey at Abomey, the capital founded on the plateau of southern Benin in the 17th century, from which twelve kings ruled until the French conquest in 1894.

Each new king built his own palace beside those of his ancestors, and their earth walls carry painted bas-reliefs that record battles and royal symbols. The kingdom grew through war and the slave trade, and the palaces held the court, the women's army and the shrines of the royal ancestors. Behanzin set the city on fire as the French advanced. UNESCO listed the site in 1985. See also Agaja and Ghezo.
